evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skips the time-boxed framing entirely. Opens with 'I'm just returning your call in regards to your move on October 10th' and immediately moves to 'Do you have just a few moments' without the 10-15 minute commitment or 'dependable quote' language. No wait for customer acknowledgment.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing began. Rep first confirmed the move address and details, then asked: 'do we have any besides pricing, questions or concerns you would like answer on this call today?' The customer immediately responds with their concern about never using a moving company before.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: When Wyatt states 'I've never used the moving company before. So I just was looking to get a quote and see what it looks like,' Brianne responds 'Okay' and moves forward. When Wyatt expands with 'we've got everything else covered. It's just some larger bulky items from upstairs which is a king mattress that's kind of floppy and then a dryer and washing machine,' rep asks 'Anything else?' Customer clarifies 'That's really. It just those three bulky items. It's in a townhome apartment. So the stairs are inside.' Rep acknowledges with 'Okay, Mm-hmm' and then the customer volunteers 'And really, that's the major concern.' Two-layer probing is present.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Rep acknowledges concerns with 'Okay' and 'Mm-hmm' but never says 'So what I'm hearing is...' or confirms the full picture.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (townhome apartment), floor (second floor), specific rooms (king mattress upstairs, dryer, washer), walking distance (8 minutes between locations), single story destination home with three bedrooms. All major logistics covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Never asked. Rep states 'we won't be moving any boxes' when learning it's a partial move, but never offers to pack items for the customer.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Never asked. Irrelevant given partial move, but not offered as an option.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gives the hourly rate ($206/hour with 2 movers and 126-foot truck) and explains inclusions, then gives a specific estimate ($585 with $70 trip fee) based on the two-and-a-half-hour minimum and the customer's move profile. However, no recognizable 'typical range for a home this size' anchor statement — the pricing jumps to specifics without establishing a comparable baseline first.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Covers trip fees upfront ('$70 trip fee to the first location'), two-and-a-half-hour minimum, fifteen-minute increments, all inclusions (fuel, truck, taxes, insurance, pads), and explicitly states 'no hidden fees of any type. So no stairwell fees, no credit card fees.' Clear fee transparency and commitment framing.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After the estimate, customer says 'Copy that it's like the minimum pricing is basically $585. Okay.' Rep responds 'Yes' and moves directly to 'I do have an 8:39 AM arrival time...' without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or pausing for customer reflection.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: None. No mention of an on-time guarantee, discount terms, or any penalty for lateness.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. Rep states: 'We do have a no worries damage coverage which is our free evaluation coverage included in the hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.' Covers the $2,000 limit, free/included framing, and no-fine-print language.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. No ask of 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. Rep simply pivots to arrival times after stating the damage coverage.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Full. Before closing, rep asks: 'do you have any other questions for me while you have me on the line.' Customer raises the couch disposal question, which is a genuine concern, not a throwaway 'any questions?' pattern.
evidence_quotes.followup_on_remaining_concern: None. Customer raises 'we have an older couch that we may or may not salvage. Do you all do like pickup of like old, discarded furniture or like trash or anything like that?' Rep responds briefly 'No, we won't take it any. Well, yeah, we can take it to like donation places but for that you're probably better off just putting it out and being like someone come get this thing.' No dig deeper or 'tell me more' follow-up.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. Rep never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' The couch question was volunteered by the customer.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full. Rep asks clearly: 'Would you like us to help you with that move on Saturday?' No softening or easy out offered.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False. No mention of 'rate lock' or that the quoted price is guaranteed.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: move date (Saturday, October 10th), phone number (implied to be on file), arrival window (12:30–2:30 PM), crew size (2 movers, 126-foot truck, $206/hour). NOT confirmed: explicit restatement of both addresses for crew notes, or notes left with the crew about the customer's stated concern (stairs with heavy items). Rep says 'I'll go ahead and send you a confirmation email with all that information' but doesn't verbally walk through the details as confirmation.

top_strength: Brianne gathered all discovery logistics cleanly and delivered detailed pricing transparency with no hidden fees disclosed upfront, which directly addressed the customer's primary concern about using a moving company for the first time.
coaching_note: Start every call with the quid pro quo framing (10–15 minute commitment, dependable quote promise, and a real pause for yes) before any probing—this call skipped it entirely and jumped into details, missing the highest-value anchor in the opening.
